description: How software and evidence together support clinical decisions: rule engines, scoring tools, alerts, literature appraisal and probabilistic diagnosis. Students build and test decision rules, appraise trials, search records and run diagnostic-reasoning cases in the lab.
modelledOn: Greenes (ed.), Clinical Decision Support: The Road to Broad Adoption
Straus et al., Evidence-Based Medicine: How to Practice and Teach EBM
Shortliffe and Cimino (eds.), Biomedical Informatics: Computer Applications in Health Care and Biomedicine
HL7 CDS Hooks and FHIR Clinical Reasoning specifications
outcomes: Implement a clinical rule or scoring tool as executable logic and test it against case data.
Design alerts that fit the clinical workflow and measure their override rate and positive predictive value.
Formulate a PICO question, search the biomedical literature and critically appraise a trial or review.
Apply sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios and Bayes theorem to update a diagnostic probability.
Evaluate a decision support tool for accuracy, calibration, safety and effect on care.

units.title: Clinical decision making and decision support
topics: Clinical reasoning: hypothetico-deductive method, pattern recognition and common cognitive biases
Types of decision support: alerts, order sets, dashboards, diagnostic aids and reference tools
The five rights of clinical decision support: information, person, format, channel and time
Decision support in Ghana: standard treatment guidelines, DHIMS2 reports and mobile tools for community health workers
History of the field: MYCIN, INTERNIST and the lessons of early expert systems

units.title: Rule-based and guideline-based logic
topics: Production rules: if-then logic, forward and backward chaining, conflict resolution
Computer-interpretable guidelines: decision tables, Arden Syntax and CDS Hooks
Clinical algorithms and flowcharts: triage, integrated management of childhood illness and malaria test-and-treat
Scoring tools: Wells score, CURB-65, APGAR and early warning scores
Knowledge engineering: eliciting, validating and maintaining a rule base

units.title: Alerts, workflow and human factors
topics: Drug-drug interaction, allergy, dose-range and duplicate-therapy alerts
Alert fatigue: override rates, positive predictive value of alerts and tiered severity
Workflow integration: interruptive versus passive alerts, timing and placement
Usability heuristics and human-factors testing of decision support screens
Safety of the tool itself: automation bias, alert errors and unintended consequences

units.title: Evidence-based medicine and critical appraisal
topics: The five steps of evidence-based practice; framing a PICO question
Study designs and the hierarchy of evidence: randomised trial, cohort, case-control, cross-sectional
Critical appraisal: selection bias, confounding, randomisation, blinding and appraisal checklists
Measures of effect: relative risk, odds ratio, absolute risk reduction, number needed to treat and confidence intervals
Systematic reviews and meta-analysis: forest plots, heterogeneity and GRADE certainty of evidence

units.title: Searching the biomedical literature
topics: Sources: PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, African Journals Online and HINARI access
MeSH headings, Boolean operators, truncation and search filters
Search quality: precision, recall and iterative refinement of a search strategy
Grey literature, preprints, retractions and spotting predatory journals
From question to answer: writing a rapid evidence summary for a clinician

units.title: Probabilistic diagnosis
topics: Diagnostic accuracy: sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive value
Bayes theorem for diagnosis: prior prevalence, posterior probability and natural frequencies
Likelihood ratios and the Fagan nomogram; chaining several test results
Test and treatment thresholds; when to test, treat or wait
ROC curves, area under the curve and choosing an operating cut-off
Decision trees, expected utility and quality-adjusted life years

units.title: Data-driven tools and evaluating decision support
topics: Risk scores from logistic regression: discrimination, calibration and Brier score
Machine-learning diagnostic aids (malaria slides, chest imaging); dataset shift to African populations
Validation: internal, external and temporal; reporting with the TRIPOD checklist
Evaluating decision support in practice: before-after, controlled and stepped-wedge designs; process versus outcome measures
Monitoring a deployed tool with queries on audit logs: firing rate, override rate and drift
Governance and maintenance: version control of knowledge, clinical ownership and retirement of rules

units.title: Standards, regulation, ethics and implementation
topics: Interoperability standards: HL7 FHIR resources, CDS Hooks, SNOMED CT and ICD-11
Regulation of clinical software as a medical device; Ghana Food and Drugs Authority guidance
Ethics: transparency, accountability, informed consent and the Data Protection Act, 2012
Low-resource deployment: offline operation, SMS delivery and decision support for community health workers
Capstone: specify, build and appraise a decision support tool for hypertension or malaria in primary care

schedule.title: How clinicians decide, and what software adds
schedule.exercise: Read two short case vignettes, name the cognitive bias in each and propose one decision support type and delivery channel that would have helped. Summarise the MYCIN lessons in half a page.

tasks.title: Work through a branching chest-pain case, recording at each step the hypothesis held and the bias risk, then compare with the model reasoning path
Choose information, person, format, channel and time for three decision support designs in a district hospital and justify each against the five rights rubric
Draw an architecture diagram showing how a community health worker tablet tool, DHIMS2 and a district pharmacy exchange data, marking where advice is generated

schedule.title: Production rules and guideline logic
schedule.exercise: Write ten if-then rules for malaria test-and-treat and trace forward and backward chaining on two patients. Convert one guideline paragraph into a decision table.

tasks.title: Code five if-then rules for fever triage in Python and run them on eight sample patients, checking each fired rule against a hand trace
Encode an hypertension treatment decision table as code, then test every row and detect missing or overlapping rule conditions automatically
Step a forward-chaining engine through an integrated childhood illness rule set, logging working memory, and find the case where two rules conflict

schedule.title: Clinical scores and knowledge engineering
schedule.exercise: Compute CURB-65 and an early warning score for six patients by hand, then review a rule base for stale thresholds and write a maintenance note.

tasks.title: Implement CURB-65 as a function and score ten sample patients, checking totals and the recommended care setting against the table
Plot early warning score against hours for a deteriorating patient, mark the trigger threshold and report how many hours earlier the alert fires than the doctor review
Review a rule base with injected errors (outdated dose, missing exception, circular rule) against evidence, scoring your fixes with the knowledge-engineering rubric

schedule.title: Alerts, fatigue and safe design
schedule.exercise: Design a tiered drug interaction alert scheme for a clinic pharmacy and predict its override rate. Sketch one passive alternative and compare.

tasks.title: Query a prescription table joined to an interaction table to list every prescribed pair with a severe interaction, and count the alerts per prescriber
Compute override rate and positive predictive value per alert type from an audit log with SQL, then recommend which alert types to suppress or demote
Run an incident case where a clinician follows a wrong alert, identify the automation-bias and design failures, and choose safeguards under the rubric

schedule.title: Evidence-based practice and study designs
schedule.exercise: Turn three clinical situations into PICO questions, name the best study design for each, and appraise one randomised trial summary with a checklist.

tasks.title: Frame a PICO question from a case about artemisinin treatment and pick the study design that best answers it from five options
Simulate a cohort with a hidden confounder, estimate the crude and adjusted risk ratio, and explain why randomisation would have removed the bias
Appraise a trial report using the checklist, rate risk of bias on each domain, and decide whether the findings justify changing local practice

schedule.title: Measures of effect and synthesis
schedule.exercise: Calculate RR, OR, ARR and NNT from two 2x2 tables, then read a forest plot and state what heterogeneity means for the pooled result.

tasks.title: Enter a 2x2 trial table and compute relative risk, odds ratio, absolute risk reduction, NNT and a 95 percent confidence interval
Pool five trial results with inverse-variance weights, draw the forest plot and compute I-squared to judge heterogeneity
Code a random-effects meta-analysis in Python, run a leave-one-out check, and report how one outlying trial changes the pooled estimate

schedule.title: Finding and summarising evidence
schedule.exercise: Write and refine a Boolean search for a clinical question, record precision and recall against a known set of relevant papers, and draft a one-page evidence summary.

tasks.title: Search a bibliographic table with SQL LIKE and Boolean conditions for a malaria question and record how many records each added term removes
Refine a search in three iterations against a gold set of 20 relevant papers, tabulating precision and recall after each version
Triage a mixed pile of trials, preprints and a retracted paper for a ward question, then submit a rapid summary scored by the appraisal rubric

schedule.title: Diagnostic accuracy and Bayes theorem
schedule.exercise: Fill a 2x2 table for a rapid malaria test, compute predictive values at 5 and 40 percent prevalence, and update a probability with two likelihood ratios.

tasks.title: Build a 2x2 table for a rapid test from 1,000 patients and compute sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV
Plot positive predictive value against prevalence for a fixed test and show why the same test misleads in a low-prevalence screening setting
Code a sequential Bayesian updater using likelihood ratios for three tests, and test its order independence on 20 simulated patients

schedule.title: Thresholds, ROC and decision analysis
schedule.exercise: Choose a cut-off from an ROC table for a blood glucose screen, set test and treatment thresholds, and solve a small decision tree for expected utility.

tasks.title: Plot an ROC curve from a table of 10 cut-offs, compute the area with the trapezoid rule and mark the point nearest the top-left
Draw a decision tree for treating or not treating suspected typhoid with probabilities and utilities, and roll it back to the best choice
Vary the cost of a missed case against a false alarm, locate the test and treatment thresholds, and chart how the best cut-off moves

schedule.title: Risk scores and machine-learning aids
schedule.exercise: Fit a logistic risk score on a small clinic dataset, check calibration, and write two paragraphs on what might break when the model moves to a different region.

tasks.title: Fit logistic regression for pre-eclampsia risk on a toy dataset and print predicted risk for five patients next to their outcomes
Plot a calibration curve in 5 risk bins, compute the Brier score and recalibrate the model, comparing before and after
Validate a risk model on a second clinic dataset with a different case mix, quantify the drop in discrimination and write a TRIPOD-style note

schedule.title: Evaluating and monitoring tools in practice
schedule.exercise: Design an evaluation of a hypertension alert in twelve clinics, choosing the outcome measures and trial design, and write monitoring queries for after go-live.

tasks.title: Write SQL on an alert audit table to give weekly firing counts and the percentage of alerts accepted, ordered by alert type
Choose a design and process and outcome measures for evaluating a sepsis alert, then defend the choice against reviewer objections in the case rubric
Detect drift in an alert from monthly firing rates with SQL window functions and propose retraining or rule retirement with the evidence

schedule.title: Standards, regulation and ethics
schedule.exercise: Map a hypertension recommendation to FHIR resources and a CDS Hooks card, then list the regulatory and ethical questions to settle before deployment.

tasks.title: Draw which FHIR resources (Patient, Observation, MedicationRequest) a blood pressure alert reads and writes, and label each with a coding system
Decide whether a given symptom-checker app is a regulated medical device and which evidence the regulator would expect, scored by rubric
Handle a case where a vendor wants patient data to retrain its model; weigh consent, data protection law and benefit, and defend your decision

schedule.title: Low-resource deployment and capstone
schedule.exercise: Present the capstone: the rule logic, the evidence behind it, the expected alert burden and an evaluation plan for a rural clinic setting.

tasks.title: Plan SMS-based advice for a community health worker with intermittent connectivity, selecting messages and fallbacks in the scenario scoring rubric
Implement the capstone rule set, test it on 30 synthetic patients and report agreement with the guideline answer for each case
Defend the capstone design before a simulated clinical governance panel, answering questions on evidence, harms, workload and evaluation
